source_rows.heading: Statement
source_rows.old_public_section: Assume AC. Let \(F\) be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary and equip it with a Riemannian metric. An open set is strongly geodesically convex if every ordered pair of its points is joined by a unique affinely parametrized globally length-minimizing geodesic whose image stays in the set and whose connector depends smoothly on the endpoints. There are finitely many such open sets \(U_1,\ldots,U_N\) covering \(F\), every nonempty finite intersection of which is strongly geodesically convex. Let \(K\) be the finite simplicial complex whose nonempty faces are the index sets \(\sigma\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}\) for which \(U_\sigma=\bigcap_{i\in\sigma}U_i\) is nonempty. Then its usual geometric realization \(|K|\) is homotopy equivalent to \(F\). For \(F=\varnothing\), take \(N=0\) and \(K=\varnothing\).

source_rows.heading: Statement
source_rows.old_public_section:
Assume countable choice. Let \(r\geq 0\), let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\) with its product Lie-group structure, and let \(M\) be a compact, finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Let \(a:T\times M\to M\) be a jointly smooth left action. Then \(M\) admits a smooth Riemannian metric invariant under \(a\). Its fixed set
\[
F=M^T:=\{p\in M:a(t,p)=p\text{ for every }t\in T\}
\]
is a compact embedded smooth submanifold with finitely many connected components, and \(T_pF=(T_pM)^T\) for each \(p\in F\). The orthogonal normal bundle \(\nu_F=(TF)^\perp\subset TM|_F\) has no nonzero \(T\)-fixed vectors in any fiber. On each connected component of \(F\), its normal representation has a finite weight decomposition into nontrivial characters of \(T\), with constant multiplicities; equivalently, \(\nu_F\) admits a smooth \(T\)-invariant complex structure and orientation on each component.

source_rows.heading: Statement
source_rows.old_public_section:
Let \(R\) be a commutative ring with identity, let \(S\subseteq R\) contain \(1\), be closed under multiplication, and not contain \(0\), and let \(0\to M'\xrightarrow{f}M\xrightarrow{g}M''\to0\) be an exact sequence of \(R\)-modules. The localization \(S^{-1}M\) is the module of fractions \(m/s\), with \((m,s)\sim(m',s')\) exactly when some \(t\in S\) satisfies \(t(s'm-sm')=0\). Then
\[
0\longrightarrow S^{-1}M'\xrightarrow{S^{-1}f}S^{-1}M\xrightarrow{S^{-1}g}S^{-1}M''\longrightarrow0
\]
is exact.

source_rows.heading: Statement
source_rows.old_public_section: Assume countable choice. Let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\) with \(r\geq1\), and let \(H\subsetneq T\) be a closed subgroup. A character means a smooth group homomorphism from \(T\) to the multiplicative unit circle \(S^1=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}\). Then there is a nontrivial character \(\chi:T\to S^1\) whose restriction to all of \(H\) is the trivial character.

source_rows.heading: Statement
source_rows.old_public_section:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let \(r\geq0\), let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\), and use \(E_T=(E_{S^1})^r\), the product of the right Milnor join models, with \(BT=E_T/T\). For the \(i\)th coordinate character \(\chi_i([t_1,\ldots,t_r])=\exp(2\pi i t_i)\), let \(L_i=E_T\times_T\mathbb C_{\chi_i}\) be the associated complex line bundle over \(BT\), with the right diagonal equivalence \((e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi_i(t)^{-1}z)\), and put \(u_i=c_1(L_i)\in H^2(BT;\mathbb Q)\). Then
\[
BT\cong(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r,\qquad H^*(BT;\mathbb Q)\cong\mathbb Q[u_1,\ldots,u_r],\qquad |u_i|=2.
\]
Every smooth character \(\chi:T\to S^1\) is uniquely \(\chi_{\mathbf n}([t])=\exp(2\pi i\sum_i n_it_i)\) for \(\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\in\mathbb Z^r\), and its associated line satisfies \(c_1(L_{\chi_{\mathbf n}})=\sum_i n_i u_i\). In particular a nontrivial character has a nonzero degree-two class. For each \(k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}\), \(H_q(BT;k)\) is finite-dimensional in every degree \(q\). For \(r=0\), \(BT\) is a point and its rational cohomology is \(\mathbb Q\).

source_rows.heading: Statement
source_rows.old_public_section: Let \(k\) be a field, let \(X,Y\) be topological spaces, and let \(f,g:X\to Y\) be continuous maps joined by a continuous homotopy \(H:X\times[0,1]\to Y\). Then \(f^*=g^*:H^n(Y;k)\to H^n(X;k)\) for every integer \(n\). Consequently every homotopy equivalence induces an isomorphism on singular cohomology with coefficients in \(k\).

source_rows.heading: Statement
source_rows.old_public_section: Assume AC. Let \(r\geq0\), let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\) use the product Milnor model \(BT=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r\) with its ordinary product topology, and let \(F\) be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. source_rows.heading: Statement
source_rows.old_public_section: Assume AC. Let \(F\) be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, equipped with a Riemannian metric, and let \(k\) be a field. There is a finite CW complex \(K\) homotopy equivalent to \(F\), and an integer \(N\geq1\) such that \(H^q(F;k)=0\) for every \(q\geq N\). Consequently the ideal \(J=\bigoplus_{q>0}H^q(F;k)\) in the graded cohomology ring satisfies \(J^N=0\). If \(F=\varnothing\), take \(K=\varnothing\), \(N=1\), and \(J=0\).

source_rows.old_public_section:
Assume countable choice. Let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\) act smoothly on a compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold \(M\) without boundary, and let \(g\) be a \(T\)-invariant Riemannian metric. If \(S\subseteq M\) is a compact embedded \(T\)-invariant submanifold, its orthogonal normal bundle \(
u(S)\) has a \(T\)-invariant open disk neighborhood \(D_\epsilon(
u(S))\) of the zero section, and the normal exponential map is a \(T\)-equivariant diffeomorphism from that disk bundle onto a \(T\)-invariant open neighborhood of \(S\). In particular, for \(x\in M\), with stabilizer \(H=T_x\), orbit \(O=T\cdot x\), and normal fiber \(V=
u_x(O)\), let \(H\) act on \(V\) by its differentials. There is an open \(H\)-invariant disk \(D_\epsilon(V)\) such that \([t,v]\), the equivalence class of \((t,v)\) under \((t,v)\sim(th,h^{-1}v)\) for \(h\in H\), maps by \([t,v]\mapsto t\cdot\exp_x(v)\) to a \(T\)-equivariant diffeomorphism from \(T	imes_H D_\epsilon(V)\) onto an open neighborhood \(U_x\) of \(O\). source_rows.heading: Definition
source_rows.old_public_section: Assume AC. Let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\) and use the product Milnor model \(ET=(E_{S^1})^r\), \(BT=ET/T\), with right diagonal action \((e,x)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot x)\). For \(k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}\), put \(A_T(k)=H^*(BT;k)\cong k[u_1,\ldots,u_r]\), where \(u_i=c_1(L_{\chi_i})\) is the degree-two class of the \(i\)th coordinate character line. For a smooth character \(\chi:T\to S^1\), set \(L_\chi=ET\times_T\mathbb C_\chi\), with the right equivalence \((e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi(t)^{-1}z)\). If \(\chi=\chi_{\mathbf n}\) for \(\mathbf n\in\mathbb Z^r\), then \(c_1(L_\chi)=\sum_i n_i u_i\). Define \(\mathscr S_T(k)\) to consist of \(1\) and all finite products of \(c_1(L_\chi)\) for nontrivial characters \(\chi\). This is a multiplicative subset of \(A_T(k)\) with \(0\notin\mathscr S_T(k)\). For a topological space \(X\) with a continuous left \(T\)-action, set \(H_T^*(X;k)=H^*(ET\times_T X;k)\), with its \(A_T(k)\)-module structure induced by \(ET\times_T X\to BT\). For an \(A_T(k)\)-module \(N\), its localization \(\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}N\) consists of fractions \(n/s\), with \(n\in N\), \(s\in\mathscr S_T(k)\), and \(n/s=n'/s'\) exactly when \(u(s'n-sn')=0\) for some \(u\in\mathscr S_T(k)\); addition is \((n/s)+(n'/s')=(s'n+sn')/(ss')\), and scalar multiplication is induced by the localized ring. The character-localized Borel equivariant cohomology is \(\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(X;k)\). For \(r=0\), there are no nontrivial characters and \(\mathscr S_T(k)=\{1\}\).

source_rows.heading: Statement
source_rows.old_public_section:
Assume AC. Let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\) act smoothly on a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable manifold \(M\) without boundary, let \(F=M^T\), and use the product Milnor Borel construction with coefficients \(k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}\). Let \(\mathscr S_T(k)\) be the multiplicative set generated by the first Chern classes of all nontrivial smooth characters of \(T\). Then
\[
\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(M\setminus F;k)=0.
\]
Equivalently, every class in the Borel equivariant cohomology of the nonfixed locus is annihilated by some finite product of nontrivial character classes.

source_rows.heading: Example
source_rows.old_public_section: Let \(T=M=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\) act on \(M\) by left translation \(t\cdot[x]=[t+x]\), and use the product Milnor Borel model with \(k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}\). This action has no fixed point. The map \([e,x]\mapsto e\cdot x\) identifies \(ET\times_TT\) with \(ET\), so \(H_T^*(T;k)\cong k\) in degree zero and is zero in positive degrees. Every positive-degree class in \(A_T(k)\) acts as zero, so localization at the nontrivial character classes gives \(\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(T;k)=0\), agreeing with restriction to the empty fixed set.
source_rows.new_public_section: Let $T=M=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ act on $M$ by left translation $t\cdot[x]=[t+x]$, and use the product Milnor Borel model with $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$. This action has no fixed point. The map $[e,x]\mapsto e\cdot x$ identifies $ET\times_TT$ with $ET$, so $H_T^*(T;k)\cong k$ in degree zero and is zero in positive degrees. Every positive-degree class in $A_T(k)$ acts as zero, so localization at the nontrivial character classes gives $\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(T;k)=0$, agreeing with restriction to the empty fixed set.

source_rows.heading: Example
source_rows.old_public_section:
Let \(T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\) act on \(M=\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1\) by \(t\cdot([z_0:z_1],q)=([z_0:e^{2\pi it}z_1],q)\), and let \(k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}\). The fixed set is the disjoint union \(F=(\{p_+\}\times\mathbb{CP}^1)\amalg(\{p_-\}\times\mathbb{CP}^1)\), with \(p_+=[1:0]\) and \(p_-=[0:1]\); the normal weights are \(+1\) and \(-1\), respectively. Let \(u\in H^2(BT;k)\) be the weight-one character class and \(b\in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1;k)\) the generator with \(b^2=0\). Then localized restriction identifies
\[
\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(M;k)\cong
\bigl(\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}A_T(k)\otimes_k k[b]/(b^2)\bigr)\oplus
\bigl(\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}A_T(k)\otimes_k k[b]/(b^2)\bigr),
\]
where the two summands are the Borel cohomology of the two positive-dimensional fixed components.
source_rows.new_public_section:
Let $T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ act on $M=\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$ by $t\cdot([z_0:z_1],q)=([z_0:e^{2\pi it}z_1],q)$, and let $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$. The fixed set is the disjoint union $F=(\{p_+\}\times\mathbb{CP}^1)\amalg(\{p_-\}\times\mathbb{CP}^1)$, with $p_+=[1:0]$ and $p_-=[0:1]$; the normal weights are $+1$ and $-1$, respectively. Let $u\in H^2(BT;k)$ be the weight-one character class and $b\in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1;k)$ the generator with $b^2=0$. Then localized restriction identifies
$$
\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(M;k)\cong \bigl(\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}A_T(k)\otimes_k k[b]/(b^2)\bigr)\oplus \bigl(\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}A_T(k)\otimes_k k[b]/(b^2)\bigr),
$$
where the two summands are the Borel cohomology of the two positive-dimensional fixed components.

source_rows.old_public_section:
Let \(T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\) act on \(M=\mathbb{CP}^1\) by \(t\cdot[z_0:z_1]=[z_0:e^{2\pi it}z_1]\). For \(k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}\), use the product Milnor Borel model and let \(u=c_1(L_\chi)\in H^2(BT;k)\) for \(\chi(t)=e^{2\pi it}\). The fixed set is \(F=\{p_+,p_-\}\), where \(p_+=[1:0]\) and \(p_-=[0:1]\); the tangent weights are \(+1\) at \(p_+\) and \(-1\) at \(p_-\). If \(\mathscr S_T(k)\) is generated by nontrivial character classes and \(A_T(k)=H^*(BT;k)\), then restriction identifies
\[
\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(\mathbb{CP}^1;k)\cong
\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}A_T(k)\oplus\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}A_T(k),
\]
with the two summands given by evaluation at \(p_+\) and \(p_-\).
